title: Epistaxis: Anterior Versus Posterior Bleeding
subject: ENT
preview: Anterior epistaxis commonly arises from the anterior septal vascular plexus.
quickRevision: Anterior epistaxis commonly arises from the anterior septal vascular plexus.
Initial measures include sitting forward, direct pressure to the soft nose and assessing hemodynamic stability.
Anticoagulants, trauma and recurrent bleeding change management decisions.

sections.title: Recognize the core pattern
points: Anterior epistaxis commonly arises from the anterior septal vascular plexus.
Posterior epistaxis is more likely in older adults and may require specialized management or airway precautions.

sections.title: Clinical examination and interpretation
points: Initial measures include sitting forward, direct pressure to the soft nose and assessing hemodynamic stability.
Anticoagulants, trauma and recurrent bleeding change management decisions.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not tilt the head backward; this can allow blood to flow into the pharynx.

quiz.question: Which first-aid step is appropriate for an uncomplicated anterior nosebleed?
options: Firm pressure on the soft nose while leaning forward
quiz.explanation: Firm pressure on the soft nose while leaning forward. Initial measures include sitting forward, direct pressure to the soft nose and assessing hemodynamic stability.
